criteria.criterion:
Content and Analysis:
the extent to which the essay
conveys complex ideas by:
• introducing a claim
• analyzing the sources and
topic
• distinguishing the claim
from alternate or opposing
claims

score_descriptors.6:
• sophisticated claim
• insightful source and
topic analysis
• insightful evaluation of
a counterclaim
score_descriptors.5:
• thorough claim
• thorough source and
topic analysis
• thorough evaluation of a
counterclaim
score_descriptors.4:
• specific claim
• appropriate source and
topic analysis
• appropriate evaluation of a
counterclaim
score_descriptors.3:
• surface-level claim
• emerging source and
topic analysis
• insufficient evaluation of
a counterclaim
score_descriptors.2:
• limited claim
• unclear or confused
source and topic analysis
• confused or no
counterclaim
score_descriptors.1:
• unrelated or no claim
• no source and/or topic
analysis

criteria.criterion:
Command of Evidence:
the extent to which the essay
supports analysis by:
• incorporating relevant
evidence from sources
• avoiding plagiarism when
citing the texts

score_descriptors.6:
• sophisticated support
using a wide range of
strategically chosen,
relevant evidence
• consistent avoidance of
plagiarism with
acceptable citation
format(s)
score_descriptors.5:
• thorough and accurate
support using effective
and relevant evidence
• consistent avoidance of
plagiarism with
acceptable citation
format(s)
score_descriptors.4:
• sufficient and adequate
support using relevant
evidence
• consistent avoidance of
plagiarism with acceptable
citation format(s)
score_descriptors.3:
• basic support using
relevant and/or
generalized evidence
• partial avoidance of
plagiarism with emerging
citation format(s)
score_descriptors.2:
• insufficient support using
limited, inaccurate, or
irrelevant evidence
• insufficient avoidance of
plagiarism
score_descriptors.1:
• provides no evidence
• no use of citations

criteria.criterion:
Coherence,
Organization, and Style:
the extent to which the essay
addresses the claim as a
cohesive, unified whole by:
• maintaining focus on task
• organizing ideas
• optimizing language style

score_descriptors.6:
• strategic focus on task
• strategic organization of
ideas
• sophisticated language
and sentence structure
score_descriptors.5:
• clear and appropriate
focus on task
• thoughtful organization
of ideas
• precise language and
sentence structure
score_descriptors.4:
• acceptable focus on task
• logical organization of
ideas
• appropriate language and
sentence structure
score_descriptors.3:
• emerging focus on task
• emerging organization of
ideas
• basic language and
sentence structure
score_descriptors.2:
• lack appropriate focus on
task, but suggest
organization of ideas
-or-
• suggest a focus on task,
but lack organization of
ideas
• imprecise language
score_descriptors.1:
• little to no focus on
task
• little to no
organization of ideas
• incoherent language
-or-
• minimal writing,
making assessment
unreliable

criteria.criterion:
Control of Conventions:
the extent to which the essay
establishes a framework for
clear communication by:
• displaying control of 9–12
band grammar, usage,
capitalization, punctuation,
and spelling
• maintaining control relative
to language characteristics

score_descriptors.6:
• exceptional control
• virtually no errors when
using sophisticated
language
score_descriptors.5:
• considerable control
• errors that do not hinder
comprehension, even
when using sophisticated
language
score_descriptors.4:
• partial control
• errors that do not hinder
comprehension
score_descriptors.3:
• emerging control
• errors that hinder
comprehension
score_descriptors.2:
• lack of control
• errors that make
comprehension difficult
score_descriptors.1:
• significant lack of
control
• errors that severely
interfere with
comprehension
-or-
• minimal writing,
making assessment
unreliable

scoring_notes: • An essay that uses information from fewer than 3 sources can be scored no higher than a 3.
• An essay that is entirely unrelated to the topic and/or makes no reference to the sources or task can be scored no higher than a 1.
• An essay that is predominantly a verbatim copy from the task or sources with negligible student writing must be scored a 0.
• An essay that is indecipherable, entirely incoherent, unrecognizable as English, or blank must be scored a 0.
